about: The cited constants of The land page's three wells (src/site/make_wells.py): each value with its source, as opened and read. The generator computes every figure the page shows from these and the well records; nothing here is typed into the page.

lift_whp_hr_per_acft_ft.source: Rogers, D.H., and Alam, M., 2006. Comparing Irrigation Energy Costs. K-State Research and Extension MF-2360 rev, p. 2: 1.373 water horsepower-hours per acre-foot per foot of lift.

hp_hr_per_kwh.source: Rogers and Alam 2006, MF-2360, p. 2: one kilowatt-hour is 1.341 horsepower-hours, so 1.373 / 1.341 kWh per acre-foot per foot at 100% efficiency (derived).

lift_kwh_per_acft_ft.source: Rogers and Alam 2006, MF-2360, p. 2: 1.55 kWh per acre-foot per foot of lift at the Nebraska Pumping Plant Performance Criteria.

assumed_drawdown_ft.source: An assumption of the page, stated on it: only a few outcrop driller's tests record a drawdown, so the outcrop pumping level uses this range.

ucm_depths_public_supply_ft.source: Texas Water Development Board, 2024. Uniform Costing Model User Guide v3.0, appendix memo (Feb. 27, 2024), Table 14, public supply wells, memo p. 30: the rows.

ucm_depths_irrigation_ft.source: TWDB UCM v3.0 memo, Table 16, irrigation wells, memo p. 32: the rows (the table stops at 2,000 ft).

ucm_capacities_gpm.source: TWDB UCM v3.0 memo, Tables 14 and 16: the columns.

ucm_public_supply_usd_2023_01.source: TWDB UCM v3.0 memo, Table 14, p. 30: cost to build and equip one public supply well, January 2023 dollars.

ucm_irrigation_usd_2023_01.source: TWDB UCM v3.0 memo, Table 16, p. 32: cost to build and equip one irrigation well, January 2023 dollars.

region_f_reindex.source: Region F Water Planning Group, 2026. 2026 Region F Water Plan, Vol. II, App. D, Table D-6, p. D-9: the 2,000 ft, 350 gpm well at September 2023 prices (1,532,046) against the same cell of the UCM memo's Table 14 (1,496,752).

enr_cci_2023_09.source: As given in the 2026 Region F plan, App. D: 'Cost based on ENR CCI 13485.67 for September 2023'.

enr_cci_2026_07.source: ENR, 'Construction Economics', July 13, 2026, p. 1: Construction Cost Index, July 2026.

bid_spread.source: TWDB UCM User Guide v3.0: the normalized standard deviation of bids, 0.35.

nrcs_well_usd.source: NRCS Texas EQIP payment schedule FY2023, p. 61, practice 642 Water Well: the payment for a well 150 ft deep or less, and 150 to 300 ft.

nrcs_pump_usd.source: NRCS Texas EQIP payment schedule FY2023, p. 46, practice 533 Pumping Plant, electric pump of 2 hp or less.

nrcs_share.source: TWDB, Funding for Private Water Wells: '75%-90% of the drilling costs can be recouped' through EQIP; the lower share gives the higher cost.

region_k_private_well_usd.source: Region K Water Planning Group, 2026. 2026 Region K Water Plan, p. 5-85: a private well at $20,000, and $27,000 per well in all (September 2023 prices).

dry_borehole_share.source: Hunt, B.B., 2008. Crystalline Basement Aquifer, Llano Uplift, Central Texas. GSA 2008 Joint Meeting, Session 805, Paper 12, abstract: about 30% of boreholes are dry.

dry_hole_cost_share.source: Daniel, C.C., III, 1990. USGS Water-Supply Paper 2341-B, pp. B30-B32, and Cederstrom, D.J., 1973, USGS Water-Supply Paper 2034: a dry hole costs roughly a fifth to a third of a finished well.

granite_example_report.source: TWDB Submitted Driller's Reports, report 524179 (Llano County, domestic, drilled October 7, 2019): the granite example, read from the 3D aquifer page's published well reports.

gravel_view_ft.source: Illustrative, rounded values of the screened gravel-and-granite view: no one report. Granite gravel saturated from a few feet to about 100 ft, with yields of 5 to 100+ gpm (Central Texas GCD Management Plan, 2023, p. 15); screens in loose material, open hole in rock (Heath 1983, USGS WSP 2220, pp. 52-53).
